verdict_summary: Phase 2 safety principles are mostly right, but the build should be reduced to a minimal paper trading kernel. PostgreSQL and Decision Gateway are necessary; premature Track B AI, full five-layer production framing, and self-built execution/data infrastructure are the main overdesign risks. Data quality and infrastructure reliability are the hidden largest risk.
top_findings: Data quality is a fatal risk: contract vs mark klines, missing real funding, base vs quote volume, and WS zero-frame incidents already blocked or invalidated work.
PostgreSQL as authoritative state is not overdesign after the Ghost Position incident; the missing part is the minimal schema, reconciliation, and restore evidence.

Decision Gateway should be self-owned as a thin risk policy seam, but exchange connectivity, order retry, and replay/live execution should be benchmarked against NautilusTrader/Freqtrade before self-building.
Track B AI analysis is correctly isolated but too early for the critical path; it should be deferred until paper ledger, monitoring, and reconciliation are stable.
Binance forceOrder is a snapshot proxy, not full liquidation tape; A-1 forward path must not claim complete real liquidation notional without third-party validation.
better_alternatives: Phase 2 minimal paper kernel: Market Data Contract + Trading Ledger Kernel + Deterministic Strategy Adapter + Decision Gateway + Paper Exchange + Reconciliation.
Run a 3-5 day spike comparing NautilusTrader, Freqtrade, and a self-built thin kernel using the same simplified carry workflow.
Add DATA_CONTRACT.yaml and data_contract_check.py before any strategy runner.
Use third-party historical data trial for liquidations, derivative ticker, funding, OI, mark/index to cross-check official/self-collected data.
Move AI Pre-Execution Analyst behind a 14-day paper zero-difference gate; keep only offline reporting before then.
notes: No Holdout read. Only the A2 audit report and this completion event were created.
